stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
The listing indicates the model is available using standard Hugging Face formats like safetensors.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Sony Music and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Major music rights holders (Sony Music and Warner Chappell) are suing AI company Anthropic.
The lawsuit centers on the alleged unauthorized use of 'tens of thousands' of copyrighted musical works by Anthropic.
The financial stakes are high, with potential damages sought up to $150,000 per work.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: Introduces CLAP, a new framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
Addresses the limitation of current video models being restricted to a single robot embodiment.
Allows models to be trained on diverse, internet-scale videos from both human and robotic agents to learn generalizable physics.

stories.title: Arbitrary code execution in QubesOS via copy-to-VM error reporting backchannel
stories.author: vntok
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability (Arbitrary Code Execution) was found in QubesOS.
The exploit leverages a copy-to-VM error reporting backchannel.
This represents a significant security flaw in a major security-focused operating system.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes key ML technologies such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It points to the use of standard NLP pipelines like 'text-generation' and core libraries such as 'transformers'.
The content is relevant to the LLM ecosystem, specifically focusing on Meta's Llama family of models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in higher quality model outputs.
The updates also lead to faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with popular local LLM runners.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated support for Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved by leveraging MLX, Apple's native machine learning framework.
This represents a significant step in optimizing local AI inference specifically for Apple hardware.

stories.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google is automatically expanding its AI search summaries (AI Overviews) on search results pages.
This expansion pushes traditional organic search links further down the results page.
The change represents a significant shift in how Google prioritizes and displays search information.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that Trump's blacklisting of Anthropic based on its stance against certain technologies was illegal.
Anthropic has publicly opposed developing lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance tools.
The ruling highlights legal challenges surrounding government attempts to influence or restrict AI development based on ethical stances.

stories.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Authorities have arrested two alleged members of the hacking group TeamPCP.
TeamPCP is known for conducting a prolific and relentless supply-chain attack campaign.
The group successfully infected over 1,000 organizations.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk posed by LLM agents in product execution harnesses, where harmful tool use is a greater threat than simple unsafe text generation.
Addresses limitations in current red-teaming methods, specifically the risk of retrieval bias in trajectory-based attack strategies.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation gap in LLMs by providing a realistic benchmark that avoids the privacy issues of internal corporate data.
Tests LLM capabilities across complex, multi-task questions using a corpus exceeding 230,000 documents.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA) to adapt advertising for Generative AI.
Shifts advertising from predefined slots to a 'generation-native' model.
Advertisers influence the generation process by reporting local continuation values to shape next-token policies.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Sophisticated generative AI tools are enabling the creation of music mimicking human artists' styles.
The rise of AI-generated music has led to an increase in unauthorized use of human artists' work.
Musicians are actively involved in efforts to combat 'AI grifters' who use or deny using generative music technology.

stories.title: Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a ‘family of devices’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma redefined 'Project Helix' from a singular console to a 'family of devices'.
This suggests Microsoft's next-generation gaming platform will likely be modular or multi-faceted.
The announcement signals a strategic shift in how Microsoft plans to deliver its next console experience.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: The article investigates the process of data deletion requests across 100 companies.
Findings indicate that privacy requests frequently result in confusion or lack of resolution.
This highlights significant friction points in current corporate data privacy practices.

stories.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta has implemented a safety feature in its AI glasses to prevent unauthorized recording.
The glasses will cease recording if the user covers the designated safety light.
This update addresses privacy concerns related to nonconsensual recording capabilities of the device.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experiences into reusable skills.
The system addresses the limitation of scattered insights in optimization histories by creating persistent, systematic knowledge.
This enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities through continuous interaction and skill refinement.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of using large-scale agent trajectory datasets for fine-tuning LLMs on software issues.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories can still contain ineffective, redundant, or risky steps, leading to noisy supervision.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance by refining supervision beyond simple task success.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Current LLM-based code review methods often treat the process as a single, static decision.
Real-world code review is inherently iterative and involves complex, multi-round interactions.
The paper introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark LLMs against the dynamic nature of actual code review.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions.
MAELLE models reactions not as molecular topology edits, but as discrete flow matching over electron occupation vectors.
This approach addresses the fundamental nature of chemical reactions as transformations in electron space.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES), an architectural pattern for LLM agents.
Addresses the conflict between allowing LLM personas to evolve freely and maintaining traceable, auditable execution.
Separates persona (which can drift) into one trust domain and execution (which must be audited) into another, connected by a governed contract bridge.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in current AI security scanner evaluation, which often only measures successful judgments.
It introduces a controlled, artifact-backed benchmark using synthetic Pickle and PyTorch artifacts.
The study evaluates three specific security scanners (ModelScan, ModelAudit, and Fickling) against a corpus of 170 artifacts.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: Addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices in modern critical care.
Presents a two-site retrospective study using large patient cohorts (totaling over 36,000 patients) to develop a new continuous sepsis severity score.
The core innovation is developing a model learned directly from patient trajectories without requiring hour-by-hour supervision.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
It moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between different moral foundations (based on Moral Foundations Theory).
The study uses six independent linear probes, one for each MFT category, to geometrically analyze the model's internal representation of these moral concepts.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of outdated, fixed-weight sepsis severity indices in critical care.
Presents a novel machine learning approach to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
Validated through a retrospective, two-site study involving over 36,000 adult patients meeting Sepsis-3 criteria.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs distinguish between specific moral foundations (e.g., care/harm, fairness).
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models, mapping these foundations geometrically.

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in large language model (LLM) pretraining, a major hurdle for academic and open-source communities.
Introduces 'Puro-2B,' a model trained using a single RTX 5090 GPU, demonstrating cost-efficient training.
Highlights the gap in accessible, hardware-friendly, and open-source LLM training recipes, contrasting with the multi-million dollar costs of larger models.

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for improving LLM reasoning.
It systematically compares ES against mainstream methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates a performance advantage of ES over GRPO in certain reasoning tasks.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to improve LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) by leveraging structured patterns in LLM failure modes across model scales.
Focuses on achieving better generalization from small language models while maintaining high computational efficiency.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experience into reusable skills.
The system addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
It enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities by systematically reusing learned skills.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the issue of noisy supervision when training LLMs on successful software resolution trajectories.
Prior methods rely on large-scale agent trajectory datasets and Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), which can be flawed.
SWE-Prime proposes a method to improve LLM performance by mitigating the risks associated with imitating ineffective or risky steps in successful trajectories.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces TTPO (Test-Time Policy Optimization) to address limitations in post-training LLM methods like RL and OPSD.
Existing test-time training (TTT) methods relying on pseudo-labels are fragile, as incorrect votes can corrupt the model.
The research specifically analyzes the asymmetric failure mode present in these pseudo-label-based training approaches.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM-based code review systems: they treat the process as a static, single-round decision.
Real-world code review is inherently iterative and interactive, involving back-and-forth dialogue between developers and reviewers.
The MCR-Bench benchmark is introduced to accurately evaluate LLMs on the complex, multi-round nature of realistic software code review.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLMs: entropy collapse leading to narrow reasoning coverage.
The proposed solution introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation to maintain the generative diversity of LLMs during RLVR.
This work aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities while preventing the degradation of performance metrics like pass@$k$ for large $k$.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to map the geometric relationships between these moral foundations.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical issue in clinical NLP: models overfitting to note-specific artifacts rather than true patient state.
Introduces CAST (Concept-guided Artifact Suppression Tuning), an SAE-based framework for making clinical text classification auditable.
Uses Sparse Autoencoders to extract human-auditable features from Transformer activations to improve model robustness during deployment shifts.

stories.title: RISC-V is now officially supported by CPython
stories.author: lumpa
bullet_points: CPython, the standard Python implementation, now officially supports RISC-V.
This integration is significant for enabling Python development and execution on RISC-V architectures.
It supports the growing trend of open-source hardware adoption and ecosystem expansion.
